skills.description: What Cryogram is, what each kind of step may do, approvals, secrets, and saying honestly what was done
How you write to the user: plain words, the result first, what was tried, and what you never reveal
When a message arrives, tell apart a question, a value, feedback on a result and a change, and do only what it asks
How to start a new workflow: save the outline, get the opening card approved, and ask only for what is missing
How to try each step for real, reuse what earlier tries saved, and keep test values apart from saved settings
What to save for later: facts about this workflow, and learnings that hold for other workflows too
How to show results, save changes to the plan, get a change or fix approved, and what must be true before you build
What a plan holds: where one step ends and the next begins, typed inputs and outputs, the lines between steps, checks, and where each value is stored
When a run failed: find the cause from what the run recorded, and tell a setup problem apart from a fault in a step
WHEN no documentation says how to call a service, and you work it out from a HAR file or from the user showing the steps
WHEN a failed run or a change needs the cases that earlier runs recorded, or a precise count across them
WHEN you design or fix a connector step: how it reaches another service, how it checks the service did what was asked, and how it sends safely
WHEN you design or fix an AI step: the prompt and what it judges by, the shape of its answer, how to try it and how to tune it
WHEN you design or fix a code step: work on this computer that gives the same result every time, such as transforming data or reading and writing files
WHEN a step reads or writes Airtable records: how to get a personal access token, how to page through records, how to write them, and what makes a request fail
WHEN a step needs a browser window on a site: how to open pages, read them, load whole lists, check you are on the right page, and reuse what earlier windows saved
WHEN a browser workflow needs the user to be signed in to a site, or a sign-in has stopped working
WHEN a step reads or writes a SQL database: how to choose between a driver and Supabase's REST address, how to store the connection string, and how to tell a temporary failure from a wrong setting
WHEN a step reads messages from a mailbox during a run: Gmail IMAP with an app password, an Apps Script bridge, or Outlook and Microsoft 365
WHEN a step reads or writes an Excel workbook in OneDrive or SharePoint: which routes are possible, and why the data must be in a named Excel table
WHEN a step sends email from a Gmail address: use a connection that already exists, or set up SMTP with an app password
WHEN a step reads or creates Google Calendar events: the secret iCal address, the Calendar API with a service account, or an Apps Script bridge
WHEN a step reads files from Google Drive or writes files to it: downloading by share link, a service account, an Apps Script bridge, and who owns an uploaded file
WHEN a step reads or writes a Google Sheet: how to choose between an Apps Script web app, the Sheets API with a service account, and the CSV export link
WHEN a step posts a message to Microsoft Teams: how to set up the webhook for a channel, a group chat or one person, and how to tell that Teams accepted a post apart from Teams delivering it
WHEN a step reads or writes rows in a Notion database: which connection to use, how to find the database's data source, and the exact shape of each property
WHEN a step reads or writes files in OneDrive: private access that is already authorised, a Power Automate bridge flow for writes, or a share link for reads
WHEN a step sends mail from Outlook or Microsoft 365: which routes fit the account type, and how to confirm that the mail was delivered
WHEN a step posts a message to Slack: how to set up an incoming webhook for one fixed channel, how to post to it, and what makes a post fail

WHEN a step calls an HTTP address the user gave you (their own service, or a Zapier, Make, n8n or IFTTT hook): how to store the address, how to send the request, and how to check that the other side did the work
